summary: El Granada sits on a coastal shelf just north of Half Moon Bay along the San Mateo County coast, which means the Pacific Ocean is not a weekend destination but a daily backdrop — visible from hillside streets, audible on still mornings, and responsible for the remarkably narrow temperature band that holds the annual average high at just 64°F and the low at 51°F, making air conditioning essentially irrelevant and heavy coats nearly so. With roughly 5,200 residents spread across 4.9 square miles at a modest density of about 1,068 per square mile, the texture is quiet-coastal rather than suburban-grid — streets wind along gentle slopes, dead-end into open hillsides, and connect to the broader Coastside Trail network that traces the bluffs southward. This is emphatically a bedroom community: almost no major employers sit on the coast side of the Santa Cruz Mountains, so commuting means threading Highway 92 over the ridge to reach the Peninsula's tech and healthcare corridors — a drive that can double in time during fog or weekend beach traffic. The median household income of $226,384 against a median home value of $1,425,800 produces a price-to-income ratio around 6.3, which is steep but notably less punishing than many Bay Area submarkets, and the median rent of $2,034 is strikingly low relative to those incomes. The tradeoff El Granada asks you to accept is geographic isolation dressed as scenery — you gain salt air and 7.8 hours of daily sunshine filtered through marine layers, but you surrender the convenience of a second grocery store or a quick errand that doesn't involve a two-lane road.
